assessment: The incumbent's reversible assembly offers an opportunity to check the ordered arrangement before dispatch, but the supplied observations do not establish that this check reliably detects component errors. Reported shortages and observed short-partition confusion suggest separate completeness and usability problems. The strongest limiting observation is D2-O6: both workers sometimes approach the eight-minute target on repeated simple orders, so uniformly slow insertion is insufficient as an explanation. Mixed-batch delays could reflect switching or layout complexity; the evidence confounds them. D2-O5 also limits a width-only explanation of insertion retries. Complaint counts and ten unpacking observations do not establish pilot success rates.

openings.claim: Does changing layout between successive orders increase selection and checking time independently of compartment count?
openings.delta: Separates transition overhead from the greater work potentially required by complex layouts, rather than attributing mixed-batch delays to either without measurement.
openings.prediction: If switching contributes materially, the same layout will take longer after a different layout than after a matching layout, particularly during selection or checking.
openings.probe: Time selection, insertion, checking and packing separately on comparable orders. Within each worker and layout, compare repeat versus changed-layout transitions, accounting for exterior color. Use only sequencing that preserves accepted specifications and delivery; otherwise use spare-board samples.
assumptions: Enough comparable transitions can be observed within available working time; otherwise the result remains unresolved.

openings.claim: The three-layout diagram leaves the short partition's role ambiguous even when all correct components are supplied; an order-specific placement diagram could improve unaided arrangement.
openings.delta: Distinguishes instruction ambiguity from missing, incorrect or difficult-to-insert components as the cause of customer difficulty.
openings.prediction: With verified identical component sets, participants receiving an order-specific diagram will more often place the short partition correctly without help.
openings.probe: Randomly assign the ten willing participants to the existing or order-specific diagram using matched, verified samples. Record correct unaided arrangement, short-partition errors and insertion failures separately. Treat results as exploratory; measure diagram preparation time and cost before adoption.
assumptions: Diagrams preserve ordered counts, colors, capacity, footprint and reversible joints.
Preparation fits the fixed deadline, 500-unit initial budget and 0.40-unit recurring allowance; this remains unverified.
